utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. We will give our ruling on the disclosure violation motion as it relates to the upcoming witness Ristic. With respect to the accused's 51st motion for finding of disclosure violation and to postpone testimony of Nebojsa Ristic and the accused's 52nd motion for finding of disclosure violation and for sanctions, the Chamber has considered the oral submissions made by Mr. Robinson and the written response filed by the Prosecution opposing the 51st and 52nd motions. Given the limited volume of material in the last batch of disclosure which pertains to Nebojsa Ristic's testimony and Mr. Robinson's estimate of the time which will be required to review that material, the Chamber is satisfied that the accused will have had sufficient time to consider this, this newly disclosed material, and incorporate it, if necessary, into his cross-examination of Mr. Ristic by the time of Mr. Ristic's scheduled testimony. Given the length and content of the new material, the Chamber is not convinced that the accused has been prejudiced by this late disclosure, although it once again reflects very badly on the disclosure practices of the Prosecution. In these circumstances, the requested postponement of or exclusion of Nebojsa Ristic's testimony is unwarranted. The Chamber will issue a full written decision in due course which addresses the other issues raised in the motions. That said, let us bring in the witness. Good morning, Ms. Gustafson. I take it that you will lead the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. If you could kindly --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning to you, sir, and to everyone present in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could take the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dzambasovic. If you could take a seat and make yourself comfortable.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Dzambasovic. If you could state your full name for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Asim Dzambasovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we could have 65 ter 90247 on the screen, please. And, Mr. Dzambasovic, do you recognise this document as an amalgamated witness statement that was read back to you in B/C/S and that you signed just a few days ago on the 18th of June, 2011?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'd just like to correct one clerical error in the statement if we could go to page 4 and zoom in on paragraph 10, please. Now, Mr. Dzambasovic, I know this is in English so I just mention the context. This is the paragraph that discusses the underground command and communications facility in Han Pijesak called Goljak. Do you recall that portion of your statement?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I recall it.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And in the middle of the paragraph there's a sentence that contains a grammatical error. The sentence reads: "I think the unit was either the 367th Communications Regiment." Could you please clarify what the name of this communications unit was?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: It was a unit of the federal secretariat for National Defence, 367th Regiment, so that part of the unit, that facility on Goljak, belonged to the 367th Communications Regiment, that entire facility belonged to that unit. That was not a unit of the 4th Corps, but rather an independent unit of the federal secretariat for National Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And with that clarification does this statement -- is this statement true and does it accurately reflect what you said at the time it was taken?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: The statement is true and it is based on my own experience, the things I saw, heard, and experienced myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if I asked you the same questions that you were asked when you gave this statement, would you give the Court the same answers that are contained in that statement?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely so, except that perhaps there would be a more detailed explanation. I -- in other words, I know far more than I put in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: With that I tender the amalgamated statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2828, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And now I'll read a summary of the witness's 92 ter statement. Asim Dzambasovic, a Bosnian Muslim, was the Chief of Staff of the 216th Mountain Brigade of the JNA from September 1990 until 6 April 1992. The commander of the 216th Brigade which was based in Han Pijesak was Colonel Dragomir Milosevic. The 216th Brigade was subordinated to the 4th Corps of the JNA, commanded by General Djurdjevac. The area of responsibility of the 216th Brigade included Rogatica, Sokolac, Vlasenica, and Han Pijesak. During late 1991 and early 1992, Mr. Dzambasovic experienced changes in the JNA and the 216th Brigade. Colonel Milosevic transferred duties away from Mr. Dzambasovic and excluded him from brigade planning. JNA units and equipment were moved to areas with a majority Serb population. For example, units were relocated from Lukavica to Sokolac and Pale. SDS leaders from Rogatica and nearby municipalities met regularly with Dragomir Milosevic in Han Pijesak. JNA weapons were distributed to the Serb population and Serb volunteers were armed, equipped, and incorporated into JNA units. A volunteer unit under the command of Rajko Kusic, a prominent Rogatica SDS member, was formed in March 1992 and placed under the command of the 1st Battalion of the 216th Brigade. His unit was responsible for terrorising mainly non-Serb civilians. Mr. Dzambasovic raised his concerns about these issues with Colonel Milosevic and General Djurdjevac. No action was taken by either officer to address these concerns. In late March or early April 1992, Mr. Dzambasovic learned about a mobilisation of Serbs. On 6 April he met with Colonel Milosevic who told Mr. Dzambasovic that he could not longer guarantee his safety. Mr. Dzambasovic then left the JNA, made his way to Sarajevo, and on 13 April 1992 reported for duty with the republican Territorial Defence. And that concludes the summary.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Mr. Dzambasovic, at the time you left the JNA and your position in the 216th Brigade, what was your rank?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: At the time I was a lieutenant-colonel.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And in your statement you describe a transformation of your treatment in the JNA in the latter part of 1991 and early 1992. For example, you discuss how you were not provided with information that you should have received, that certain duties were taken away from you, and that non-Serb officers felt insecure, and I refer to paragraphs 57 and 82 of the statement. My question for you is: Did you discuss these issues, either at the time or later on, with other non-Serb JNA officers; and if so, how did their experiences in the JNA compare with yours?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: When I had occasion to, I did, not only with officers from my own brigade but also from officers from other units of the 4th Corps. On several occasions I personally went to Lukavica, which is the garrison where I had been posted before my arrival -- before my move to Han Pijesak, and I knew a lot of officers there. And I discussed this issue with them as well and they most -- most of them had the same opinion as mine or similar.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if we could have 65 ter 23158 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Mr. Dzambasovic, do you recognise this map as a map of Rogatica municipality that you made some markings on a few days ago?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I recognise both the map and most of the places indicated there.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now, this is -- this map is discussed at paragraph 123 of your statement. I'd just like to ask a couple of further questions. In the -- just above the centre and just to the right of that, so in the upper right-hand quadrant of the map, there's an oval-shape circle around the village of Borika. Is this the area that you marked in which Rajko Kusic's unit operated as you describe in your statement?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: That is the central part -- territory of his activities. However, the wider area is the area where he conducted patrols, Borika-Rogatica, Borika-Visegrad, and Borika-Zepa, those were the routes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And at the time of this map above Rogatica you've marked where the municipality of Han Pijesak appears just at the very top of the map. Which ethnic group was in the majority in Han Pijesak in 1991, if you know?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I do know that perhaps not with absolute precision, but I know the Serb population had the majority.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I tender that map, Your Honours, and I note that we are waiting a translation of the B/C/S text that appears above the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are you suggesting to mark this for identification pending that translation?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll do that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI P2829, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if we could have 65 ter 07951 now on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now, this is a report of the 1st Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade to the Drina Corps command dated the 25th of February, 1993, and signed by Rajko Kusic. This report, Mr. Dzambasovic, is discussed in some detail at paragraph 119 of your statement. So I'd just like to ask one or two questions about it today.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: If we could go to page 2 of this document in both languages. And if we could focus on the top third of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And approximately -- starting on the third line down there's a passage that begins: "At that time a group of about 40 Serbian young men, SDS activists, returned to Rogatica municipality and volunteered to attend courses for anti-sabotage activities in education centres in Pazaric, Pancevo, and Han Pijesak, taught by patriotic JNA officers. That unit was the first organised formation of Serbian army in Rogatica municipality and it was deployed on plateau Borika from the 3rd of March, 1992." Now, Mr. Dzambasovic, to what extent is that information in the report consistent with the information you had at the time about the formation of Rajko Kusic's unit?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: This information that is presented by Kusic as unit commander absolutely correspond with the information that I provided to you in my statement. There's only one difference in view of a particular date. Here it says the 3rd of March, but the arming of the unit and the establishment of the unit actually took place in Gucevo on the 4th of March, 1992, so there's just this one day of difference but that doesn't really matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you could just look on the same page about four lines down from where I just finished reading, there's a passage that begins: "During that time SDA armed forces introduced terror and genocide against Serbian people of Visegrad municipality." And two lines further down it reads: "Immediately after Visegrad, SDA armed formations from Rogatica municipality started their activities as follows: Maltreating Serbs and preventing them to join their working places, killing of soldier on leave, Mihajlovic Drazen, and attempting to kill villagers of Mandra in Borika area. All this led Serbian people to confront Ustashas in the armed conflict and undertake certain military activities as the freedom of movement for the Serbian people was rapidly decreasing and the normal life was no longer possible." Based on your knowledge of the situation in Rogatica and the surrounding municipalities at the time, is this report on the threat by SDA armed forces against Serbs accurate?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: The facts referred to in this report are absolutely inaccurate. I personally talked to the representatives of the government in Rogatica, or rather, of the Serb people, specifically with Mr. Batinic and Vujic, and I never heard that they had any problems whatsoever in terms of being terrorised by the Muslim people in any way. However, we had a lot of complaints from the organs of government and the Muslims, that it was the Serbs who terrorised people in many areas and that that, indeed, had happened. So these facts are actually the other way around. If they are honest, the top people of the SDS in Rogatica can confirm this as well, the persons I talked to at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I tender this report, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2830, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Mr. Dzambasovic, in your statement you described in some detail the arming of the Serb population and Serb volunteers in the Rogatica area, and I refer to paragraphs 41 through 75. At the time that you left the JNA in early April, are you able to tell the Trial Chamber to what extent the Muslim population in Rogatica and its surroundings was armed compared with the Serb population?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I personally never went -- never dealt with that problem so I do not know the actual statistics involved. However, what I do know from my conversations with many people, that is to say they had hunting weapons, those who had them legally, and also they had some personal weapons, as in military weapons that they had bought at the time, assuming - well - there would be a crisis and what actually did happen later would happen. Now, I would not know anything more specific than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: So just to get back to my question, are you saying you're not able to provide a comparison of the level of arming of the Muslim population versus the Serb population?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: The Serb population was armed by the JNA, almost fully. Compared to that, the Muslim population was not armed. So these statements are absolutely correct, the extent to which somebody was armed or unarmed. I said that I did not know the actual numbers involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And in paragraphs 76 to 79 of your statement, you explained that after the second mobilisation in September 1991, the relationship between the Serb officers in your brigade and the SDS was that of a brotherhood. And you described how SDS officials from Rogatica and surrounding municipalities would frequently visit with Colonel Milosevic at the barracks. Now, my question for you is: Did Colonel Milosevic hold any similar meetings with politicians of other parties to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, there were no meetings with politicians of other parties. However, what happened primarily had to do with Srebrenica, Vlasenica, Olovo, Kladanj. Activists of the SDS, they came to the barracks and that was a precedent in army practice up until then. That is what we, as professional soldiers, did not consider normal, to see political representatives coming into army barracks and asking for whatever.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And what message, if any, did this -- these activities and this relationship send to you about the role of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I personally, since I was Chief of Staff, that is to say, ex officio deputy commander of the brigade, felt that the most. Whenever I had an opportunity, I discussed that with Commander Milosevic. I also talked to the corps commander to bring this practice to an end if we are the JNA as such. If we are going to honour the principles of how a military organisation should function, then this practice has to be brought to an end; however, that never happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: That concludes my examination-in-chief and I'd just like to tender the associated exhibits other than the two that have been admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Any objections, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. They will be admitted and given numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And, sorry, Your Honour, one final matter. I've just been informed by Mr. Reid that we now have a translation for MFI P2829, if that can be admitted now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The legend of the map?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we take your word and that will be admitted in full.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, before we commence the cross-examination, I want to alert the Chamber that a part of the cross-examination -- in fact a great part of the cross-examination will relate to this witness's ability to give evidence relevant to our case concerning the events in Sarajevo. And Dr. Karadzic will be then proceeding under Rule 90(H)(i), which allows him to ask questions other than those which are contained within the scope of direct examination and I just wanted to alert you to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Dzambasovic, and at the same time I wish to express my gratitude to you for having met with me and my associates before testifying here. So I believe that that will help us in avoiding any kind of lack of clarity.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Briefly I would like to remind you of what you said on different occasions so far. For example, in the Kupreskic case, transcript page 1255 [as interpreted], you say - and that was on the 29th of February, 1999 - that at the beginning the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina had a lack of clothing, so they fought against the Serbs wearing their own civilian clothes; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. For the most part that was correct in the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You also said, for instance, in your statement of September 2002 and October 2002, paragraph 6 and paragraph 1, that, for instance, officers who were non-Muslims, or rather, who were Serbs went to these areas. And I asked you during our interview whether it was customary, for example, that in Belgrade, a Macedonian was commander of the military district, like Apostolski, and then Avramovic, a Serb in Zagreb elsewhere, and so on?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, as the army functioned from Slovenia to Macedonia, that's the way it was. However --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll get to that, we'll get to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. What's the date of his first statement in Kupreskic case? 1999?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 95-16-T, page 12255.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then you said in your statement of September 2002 - October 2002 on page 11, 30, 41, paragraph 9, 11, 342, that in 1990 in September the JNA in a way tried to restrict the Territorial Defence by way of the decision of Bajcetic, commander of the Territorial Defence, that the arms of the Territorial Defence be entrusted to the JNA, and you interpreted that as an attempt to disintegrate the Territorial Defence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: That is an official document, that is to say, of the republican TO staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: That's all right, Your Honour. The question was answered. I was just going to ask for a precise quote from that statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I proceed? So this was an official document of the commander of the republican staff of Territorial Defence. We professional soldiers, at the moment this arrived in JNA units -- actually, the explanation given to us was that this was a document that had to do with rationalisation, not to keep weapons in a single -- in two different locations but in a single one. From a certain point of view that was rational and normal, if you have two depots and then now you have one. However, that was not the intention of this weapon transfer, it was the other way around. The JNA wanted to control everything, all equipment, all weapons, so that at some point in time they would be the only ones that were able to use these weapons, that is to say, only the JNA not the Territorial Defence units in the area where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What I'm waiting for is the interpretation. So I would like to ask you kindly to pause a bit between my question and your answer so that it can be interpreted. Was this issued on the 13th of September, 1990, and was that almost three months, or rather, two months before the first multi-party elections? Was that done by the old socialist, or rather, communist government?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly when the elections were held. I don't know the exact dates. If that was so, then yes. If the elections took place later, then that was done by the Territorial Defence, or rather, the republican leadership of the TO and the JNA, the old ones as you had put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was your interpretation of this an assumption that they were afraid of the outcome of the multi-party elections and that they wanted to place arms under their own control?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we in the army, generally speaking, were against such elections. On the basis of what people did not know but intimated that there would be this corralling into mono-ethnic enclosures, and that is what we found unacceptable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then in your statement of September/October 2002 in paragraph 4, and then in paragraph 3 as well, you confirmed that the SDA and the SDS obstructed mobilisation, saying to reserve officers and soldiers that they should not respond to mobilisation call-up and that even the police obstructed mobilisation in a way; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: This was an absolute precedent and that is indeed what happened. Both leaderships, both the Muslim and Serb leadership at the time of this first mobilisation obstructed this mobilisation. This was officially confirmed by the leadership of the command of the 4th Corps in the report on the realisation of this mobilisation, and I think that you have that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Dzambasovic, if I could remind you again that you need to put a pause between the question of Mr. Karadzic and your answer so that the whole conversation could be interpreted into the working languages of the Tribunal, please. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the JNA had their own assessment of the political developments and that they based those assessments, or rather, that they had these assessments about why there was this kind of attitude toward mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: The JNA always made assessments and evaluated the situation. In every scenario of planning, the former JNA also took into account the issue of the political situation in the area of responsibility and that in -- from the highest level up to the lowest levels.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement of 13th June 2000, in paragraph 7, you confirmed, or rather, you stated that the political leadership of the SDA and the SDS obstructed mobilisation, in late June 1991, or rather, the 29th of June, 1991, and that only 60 per cent of people who received the call-up actually responded?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Those figures and percentages, I really don't know them off the top of my head but if that's what I said then that's what it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the same statement in paragraph 6 you state that that came as a surprise to you, the mobilisation itself, because in your assessment it was expensive, complicated, and it disrupted the everyday life of people. And you said that that kind of mobilisation would be normal in major crisis, but that you did not consider that your country was in such a crisis at that point in time. What did you mean by "your country"?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: What I meant by "my country," I meant specifically the area of responsibility of my unit, which is five to six municipalities, Rogatica, Vlasenica, Han Pijesak, Sokolac, and we assessed that it was not justified to mobilise the whole brigade because we had already had mobilisations before that but it was only a military exercise. And when this came about we also considered it to be a military exercise. However, on this occasion the entire brigade was mobilised, which means all its resources, human, technical, materiel, everything had to be mobilised and that was way too expensive and too complicated. And we did not believe that there were reasons justifying that kind of mobilisation at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At this time in Yugoslavia, was there an emergence of a new element when Croatia and Slovenia declared their independence and the conflict in Slovenia began?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. This was at a time when the conflict in Slovenia broke out, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that at that time Slovenia took control of the outer borders of Yugoslavia, the outer borders that were on Slovenian territory?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall the TV programmes that we watched and also I remember the reports that we received. Practically Slovenia's TO took control of its borders and the JNA then took their own steps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If we were to assume that your country was Yugoslavia and not the Romanija-Birac region, would your position then have been different? So if Yugoslavia was in jeopardy, would there be reason enough for mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in theory that's correct. However, our unit was not a large unit, not in terms of the entire Yugoslavia. So had the 4th Corps been mobilised, the entire 4th Corps, and had we been told that this was the crisis in question then perhaps that would have been justified. However, this was done at a local level and in such a way that we in fact never received a specific mission. So that was totally absurd. On the one hand your entire unit was being mobilised, and on the other hand you had no idea why that was the case, and that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you yourself could not draw a parallel and a conclusion that because of the crisis in Slovenia that's why this was done?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we could only assume that; however, neither in theory nor in practice was it ever the case that we would not know what our assignment was. And on this particular -- in this particular situation we never received any specific assignment. And then when we went with part of our unit to Zaluzani near Banja Luka, again we had no idea why we were doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you were moved, transferred to the west, towards Slovenia, in other words, because Banja Luka is some 200 to 300 kilometres to the west, closer to the fighting in Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, well certainly it's closer to Slovenia than Sarajevo, by all means.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that up until the second mobilisation at the end of July 1991 the SDA and SDS still had the same position vis-a-vis the JNA and they were not inclined to support it; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, you could say it that way. At that first -- during that first period in June and July, well, one could say that there was general chaos both at the political and the military levels.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then there was an occurrence where representatives of the SDA went to Zaluzani and re-called their supporters from the brigade that were posted in Zaluzani; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct. At that time, representatives of the SDA from two municipalities, Rogatica and Vlasenica, arrived there and all those members who did respond to mobilisation, they re-called them, they put them on buses. These people left all their weapons there in the meadows on the side of the road, they got on the buses, and went back home.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please pull up -- please bear with me. I would like to show you a document on ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Could I just ask if this is in the list of cross-examination documents; and if so, a reference number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid it is not; however, if you do object we can tender it on another occasion. I just want to show it to the witness to -- because of something that he has said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this a document from the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Executive Council of Vlasenica, dated the 8th of July, 1991, whereby our joint Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina is being informed that, in early morning hours, citizens gathered in the area of Vlasenica outside the city hall for mobilisation purposes. And it says that the Municipal Assembly had provided transportation and the -- they organised transportation for those people who were mobilised to be returned home. Is this the document that is referring to that same event?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, I would say think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we tender this with an MFI?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Obviously, Your Honour, we have no ability to review this document at this time. If we could reserve any objections we might have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark this document for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1373, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then in your statement of the 22nd, or rather, the September/October statement of 2002, in paragraph 3 you say that Muslims in July and then in September during the second mobilisation drive, Muslims and Croats boycotted the mobilisation or that they responded in order to return the weapons that had been issued to them; is that the case?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Well, basically there was some political decisions that were made then, and as of September the response of Muslims and Croats to call-ups was practically non-existent or very, very small.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The crisis in Slovenia had by that time abated a little; however, it had now moved to Croatia where there were blockades of various barracks and so on; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. As far as I know there were several instances where several barracks in Croatia were blocked by protesters. I don't know exactly at what time that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You then go on to say that on the 17th of September - and you stated that in your statement of 13th June, 2000 in paragraph 6 - that they -- that old plans had to be ignored and new plans had to be established -- had to be developed because the old plans had anticipated threats from NATO or the Warsaw Pact, whereas the situation on the ground was now different; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. That was the major upset that happened then. Whenever a war-time plan was drawn up, it was the practice in the army that the Chief of Staff together with his staff developed this plan and the assignment would always be received from a superior command. However, on this occasion I was told by my commander that all those old plans had to be scrapped and that new plans have been drawn up. In other words, I was totally excluded from the planning, as well as all other officers who were non-Serb. I never saw the content of those plans, I didn't know what they contained, and I don't know that to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, we will get to the issue of distrust or trust that they had in you, but let's move on now. In the same statement, paragraph 7, you say that it was almost exclusively Serbs who responded to this call-up and that this upset the ethnic balance in the JNA and that it was only then in September 1991 that the SDS and the JNA began drawing closer together, or rather, could we say that the JNA was increasingly seeking support from the Serbian ethnic group and asking for their assistance in mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I said that during the first mobilisation the position of the SDS and SDA were the same as far as mobilisation was concerned; however, during the second mobilisation their positions have changed. The SDS was in full support of the JNA and mobilisation at this time, so that is where the difference arose, that's where the positions changed. And that is something that I mentioned a little earlier when I said that SDS leaders from these municipalities which were in the area of responsibility of my brigade came to me announced and unannounced at all times of day and had contacts and meetings with Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, Your Honour, I just wanted to point for the record that the previous question referring to plans in anticipation of threats from NATO or the Warsaw Pact mis-characterised the witness's prior statement. It took me some time to find it because the reference given by Mr. Karadzic was incorrect. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. You can move on, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's the statement from 2000, paragraph 5 one of these matters and 6 the other one. But basically -- yes, paragraph 6. Basically -- actually, can you confirm that all the way up until that moment the entire military doctrine, the doctrine of Yugoslavia, counted on threats coming either from NATO or from the Warsaw Pact and that these plans had become useless and changed; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in this specific case in terms of what happened, that is true. Until 1991, the JNA had war plans that included elaborated plans in case of an aggression either by NATO or the Warsaw Pact, so that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you mentioned these contacts now between the local authorities and the JNA, let us establish one thing. In that zone was it the SDS and the SDA that were in power? Was there power-sharing in these municipalities where you were?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: In all these municipalities -- well, it depended. Where there was a majority Serb population, Serbs held most of the important offices and the other way around, so that is correct. That is how they functioned. Now, I don't know the exact date when all of these authorities were split up like the MUP and everything else, the Serb and the non-Serb, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: For example, in Rogatica the president of the municipality was a Muslim and Serb was the head of the Executive Council; right -- [No interpretation]?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the end of the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know who his deputy was but I don't know whether he was a Muslim, but the majority population in Han Pijesak was Serb, so I think both the chief and his deputy were Serbs and there was a Muslim in the Executive Board. I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in your statement from September 2002 in paragraph 5 you said that Kusic was a volunteer in the army at that point in time and that he had not been mobilised, rather, he volunteered?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Exactly. I had never heard of Kusic or seen him until then. He appeared -- well, I don't know exactly how many times and I don't know how much that matters anyway, but very often he appeared as some representative of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Representative of the SDS or the representative of the local authorities?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, probably it is the local authorities from the area that he came from. I don't know which particular offices people held and that was not exactly my line of work, so that's what I have to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Further on, you say in your statement of September 2002, paragraphs 5 and 6, that in 1991 and in early 1992, Milosevic, then-Colonel Milosevic, heard that in Vares the neighbouring municipality, the HOS was established, the Croatian armed forces. And he disguised himself as a medical person and went out to reconnoitre; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he told me. In the building of the municipal staff that is on the outskirts of Vares, I didn't go there, there was a unit with HOS insignia and he said that he went in an ambulance dressed as a doctor or a nurse to that particular area to reconnoitre and that is what he established.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, again that statement does not appear in paragraphs 5 and 6 of the 2002 statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But the witness confirmed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It just makes our job much more difficult if we don't get accurate references.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I have no means to check whether it's correct or not, but please be precise in giving references, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, please give me enough time and then I'm going to be very precise, but that is contained in this paragraph, that the HOS was established and that Milosevic disguised himself as a doctor and went out to reconnoitre, that is contained somewhere else. But we don't have enough time, so I am actually summarising and I'm kindly asking Mr. Dzambasovic, who has been very kind to us, to confirm but I really don't have time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then would you be happy, Ms. Gustafson, if Mr. Karadzic just asked questions without giving any reference?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You confirmed that, in the beginning of 1992 in Central Bosnia, Muslim armed forces were established, the so-called M-O-S, MOS; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I told you that that was a unit that was formed. I don't know the exact date officially, but you do have this document. They were established in the territory of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The previous question, the H-O-S, the Croatian armed forces, do you remember that that armed formation was established by the extremist Croatian Party of Rights that is an heir to the Ustashi traditions of the Second World War?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as regards all these names that were being used from the Second World War, that is what the JNA called them, all of those who were against us in the Second World War. So this HOS is included.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please try to understand why I am waiting. I am waiting for the interpretation and you can follow it yourself and you can wait for it to finish. This formation, the MOS, who did it report to?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: According to the documents I saw, it was the 3rd Corps of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And before the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was established, who did it report to? Because you said that they were formed in the beginning of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, only God almighty knows that. I never went in there, never saw that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During the interview I asked you and at the time you could not remember information about the Patriotic League, when it was established exactly and how it was organised. Can you remember more today?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: As far as the Patriotic League is concerned, I really don't know anything. I was not involved in this organisation in any way or from then until the present day did I attend any meeting that had anything to do with that. Quite simply, I didn't want to do anything in that connection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about the JNA and the intelligence service of the JNA, were they following this mass organisation called the Patriotic League? Did you hear of this kind of monitoring and analysis?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: As a JNA officer, of course I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you hear that in September 1991 the SDA passed a decision on the active monitoring of everything that was happening in the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: No. This is the first time I hear of it, so it is only right this moment that I know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that such activities are forbidden by the Law on Defence and the Army and the Law on All People's Defence? I'm not asking you to confirm that they were doing that, but is it not generally known that that is forbidden, spying on the army?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's a question that is both complicated and simple. All armies in the world are being spied on and it is forbidden to spy on any army in the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then you stated that meetings were held in February 1992 between the minister of the interior, Alija Delimustafic; the chief of state security of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Branko Kvesic; Delimustafic's deputy, Vitomir Zepinic; then-Colonel Vasiljevic; Tumanov; Simic; and Colonel Milosevic. And then, as you said, they divided up tasks between the JNA and the MUP and it was Aleksandar Vasiljevic who informed you about that, he was a colonel then. Is that correct, that in February 1992 they were involved in the same mission, the same task, the army and the MUP?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I was not present at the meeting itself that was held, but I was there in that particular location. As for Aco Vasiljevic, I had a very close relationship with him because for a while he was my commander. As we were having coffee he told me that they tried to regulate obligations with the MUP by way of providing for the safety of citizens through the establishment of joint patrols that would include representatives of the army and representatives of the MUP. From time to time these patrols would go to trouble spots in that area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that when there was a lack of manpower in the JNA the Presidency of the SFRY reinforced their decision on the right to involve volunteers in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: At the time I did not have very specific information, except that Milosevic had informed me that this method would be applied, namely, that volunteers would be taken into army units. Later on I saw documents supporting that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that in our system every reserve officer and every reserve soldier had his war-time assignment and was considered to be a soldier in the reserve who could be called up or who could volunteer if there were to be a war crisis?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the Law on National Defence and on military obligation regulated that in detail. I'm not aware of each and every detail right now, but that was the way it was. All of those who were of military age and were able-bodied were deployed in various units. Those who were not able-bodied were in the civilian protection and in other units in order to help in possible crises.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Or were supposed to have work obligation as their own war obligation; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: There was that possibility too, work obligation in case there was a crisis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Further on you say that towards the end of March, from the 24th until the 26th, a crisis broke out in Rogatica. Roadblocks were set up and they were removed at the intervention of Colonel Milosevic; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: These roadblocks were placed in the second half of March. In relation to that, the political leadership from Rogatica provided us with information and the corps commander, General Djurdjevac, and from my brigade it was Milosevic and myself, we went to Rogatica. We held a meeting with the leadership of the municipality. They informed us about the situation in detail. And then practically we went out to remove the roadblocks. The first roadblock was the one that was placed by the Muslims, and then about 500 metres away from that, on the road leading from Rogatica to Borika on the bridge, there was a Serb roadblock. This roadblock that was placed by the Muslims, they removed straight away, as soon as I walked out. It was just formal. When we came to the barricade that was placed by the Serbs - maybe I should put this in soldierly fashion - the soldiers that were around the roadblocks, Serb soldiers, they threatened us a bit. And then Milosevic got out of the car, went up that hill where the army had been deployed, spoke to Kusic, came back, and half an hour later the Serbs removed their roadblock as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Today on page 8 of today's transcript you confirmed that as for the area of responsibility of your brigade the young men who were trained in Pazaric, Pancevo, and Han Pijesak had returned to it. Is Pazaric basically 100 per cent Muslim; and the infrastructure in Pazaric, Pancevo, and Han Pijesak, did that belong to the JNA?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. First of all, I think that you did not word the very beginning properly. Could you just repeat what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On page 8 you confirmed that at the time -- actually, you confirmed what was written by --

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: -- what Kusic wrote in his report, that at the time these young men came back, those who had trained in Pazaric, Pancevo, and Han Pijesak. The first question: Is Pazaric practically 100 per cent Muslim populated?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Pazaric is a very small local commune. Its population is about 1500. Since that was a training centre for all units that were completing the military academies in Sarajevo, yes. As for the structure of the population itself, it was majority Muslim. I asked you to correct what you said because it wasn't me, I didn't write that. That's what Kusic wrote in his report, and I confirmed that that was a training centre, Pazaric is, Pancevo is -- or rather, they were, in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Here you also state that the Zepa commander, Avdo Palic, Lieutenant-Colonel Avdo Palic, informed you of his contacts and meetings and my arrival, my and Dukic's visit to Han Pijesak, and the movement of the political leadership; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Avdo Palic at the time was a member of our command; he was an artillery officer. And at this time when government representatives who, as I had already mentioned, began to work closely with the JNA and since he was in Han Pijesak at the time -- in that area at the time, he informed me in Han Pijesak on several occasions that you and Rajko Dukic went there on a couple of occasions where you held some meetings but he didn't know what those meetings were about, nor did I.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where were those meetings held, with whom?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, with Commander Milosevic, but I don't know exactly where it was, whether it was in Han Pijesak or elsewhere, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the one hand you say that you knew that Colonel Milosevic was distrustful of you, and on the other hand Avdo Palic trusted you, as well as other officers, non-Serb officers - and this is what you said on pages 5 and 6 of today's transcript and you confirmed it today - when you said that other non-Serb officers came to you to inform you of their concerns.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, that's totally logical and it's correct. Milosevic and I were on very good terms up until the first mobilisation. We went out together every evening, we took walks. After that, when what happened happened, I can say that he did not dare go out with me anymore, not because he was afraid of me but because he was banned from doing that or he was -- there was a ban imposed on him from doing that by the Serb people.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now briefly take a look at 1D3708.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this a document from the 4th Corps command, the security organ is sending information on what they learned about the activity of the SDA in the territory of Han Pijesak, and this was on the 30th of October, 1991; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, if that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. They inform here that they had a conversation with Jusuf Jusufovic. Did you know this man?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I knew the man personally. For a while he was the chief of the municipality and for a while Milosevic and he and I were friends together, and even during the euphoric period when weapons were being distributed he was one of those that got a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that this Jusuf Jusufovic felt unsafe because of his pro-Yugoslav stance and that's why he was issued a weapon for his own personal protection?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, listen, that's how it was at the time. There were individual people, Muslims, Serbs, or Croats, at the time who had a different take on everything, they had a different view of the situation of -- or rather, their views departed from what had happened during the multi-party elections. And all those people were in jeopardy of sorts, they were unsafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please take a look at the part of the report where it refers to the situation in Rogatica and Vlasenica on villages that wanted to establish a new municipality and then that the SDA leadership had numerous contacts with Osman Brka and Irfan Ajanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And then could we have the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the JNA is referred to here -- that the JNA's here in fact pointing out these people: Salih Mehovic, Muhamed Kuc, Himzo Mujkic, Mehmedalija Memisevic, Jusuf Ivojevic, Enes Jusupovic - not the Jusuf Jusufovic - that they point them out as extremists here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now can we have the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of these assessments of the people?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you answer. Yes, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I heard a question there and I'm not sure the witness had the chance to read the page and answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like to read that document again, the previous page, or are you following the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did understand the essence by looking at this; however, unfortunately, this document, since it was produced by the JNA, we should have been the first to receive it, we the people in the unit and this is, in fact, the first time that I see it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we just scroll down to the end so that we see whose signature appears there. That's on the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know a Lieutenant-Colonel Petar Simovic? Was he in the intelligence service of the 4th Corps?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I know him personally. He too attended a meeting where Tumanov, Vasiljevic, Delimustafic, and the others that we mentioned a moment ago were, so I know him personally, I know Simovic personally. He was the chief of security.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we see the first page. Mr. Dzambasovic, I take it this is a report of information written by security service in the JNA corps command. Did the -- did a Chief of Staff in a brigade receive all the reports written by the security service in the corps command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this report was drafted by the 4th Corps command. However, the information contained in it came from my assistant for security, the assistant in my brigade. This happened in the area of responsibility of the 216th Brigade, all of the events mentioned here. My organ or the individual in the brigade who was in charge of security was supposed to inform me of this and of course then forward this report, as he did. And in fact, this is the first time that I see it, this report. My assistant, my organ, was not Lieutenant-Colonel Simovic, it was a captain --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- it was his responsibility to show me a document of this nature and then forward it to the command, whereas here we see that this document is sent by the 4th Corps command as information, as a report. I don't know if this is sufficient by way of answering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then my question is again whether a report by the security in the brigade go through a Chief of Staff or commander of the brigade to the upper level security organ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand your question. The security organ reported to the commander, or rather, the Chief of Staff. It could forward the information without informing -- without our knowledge. However, he would have to inform us subsequently that he had done that. In other words, he could send, as a security organ, independently a report to his superior security organ, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Back to you, Mr. Karadzic -- I note the time. It's time to take a break. And we'll have a break for half an hour and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't see the witness. I was told that, Mr. Karadzic, you have something to raise with us.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you for giving me this opportunity. I'd like to say, or rather, to remind you that I agreed that General Karavelic's statement should be admitted because at that point in time he was on the list of Prosecution witnesses. However, once the statement was admitted, the Prosecution withdrew the witness and it was transformed into a 92 bis. This witness here is our last opportunity to hear from a commander of the BH army about the developments in Sarajevo, what the balance of forces was, and what the circumstances were. It is based on this that I am seeking additional time because the Defence could find this witness's evidence helpful. The question of time is a great obstacle for the Defence. I do make a lot of errors because I try to shorten my questions and I try to do as much as possible in as little time as possible, and it is to my detriment more often than not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Two questions. I didn't follow your comment on General Karavelic's statement. Probably Prosecution can help us. In what context did we admit that and could -- do you have that number for that -- or Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can do that. I offered one passage from the statement where General Karavelic states that the Sarajevo Romanija Corps engaged artillery just as his 1st Corps did. The Prosecution then tendered the entire statement into evidence. Now, since this witness was on the list of the coming witnesses, I did not oppose the application. Now, once the Prosecution got -- once their application based on 92 bis was granted, they withdrew the witness. And this witness here who is now testifying is a senior officer of the BH army and he's one of our last opportunities to talk to and elicit information on what the events in Sarajevo were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'll come to the second issue. Yes, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just on the point of General Karavelic's statement, if Your Honours please, Ms. Edgerton knows more about that than I do if she could address the Court on that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure she knows the issue. I think it arose in recent days, but I don't think that has direct relation to this issue. I'll come to this issue. I read this witness's 92 ter statement, but nowhere I found what he did during the war. But you referred to him as being a commander of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you confirm that, Ms. Gustafson?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And you're correct, that none of that evidence appears in his statement because that's not the reason that we called the witness and that's not the topics that we elicited from him, but it is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But as a commander of the ABiH he may be able to answer questions in relation to Rule 90(H) questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: He may, Your Honour. And we leave it in the Court's hands. I just point out that, because this is an entirely new topic that is not covered in the evidence that the Prosecution elicited, it's very short notice for us to deal with these new topics and the documents. And if the accused would like to do this in the future I think it would be fair that we have some advance notice that this will be done and of the documents that will be used on these topics falling under 90(H). Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you know what rank and what position he took during the war, what commander he was?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I believe at some point, the point the accused is interested in, he was the Chief of Staff of the 1st Corps of the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the rank?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: At some point he became a general, but I can't confirm when.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may respond and explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Starting from late 1992 up until autumn of 1993, the witness was the Chief of Staff of the 1st Corps. In the course of the interview he was kind enough to make certain markings on our maps that we would like to present here today. I think this should have been a clear indication enough of our interest in these matters, all the more so since the list of Prosecution witnesses does not include Mr. Karavelic any longer. He's been transformed into a 92 bis witness and there are no other witnesses on their list who could testify to these issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In addition to this session, how much longer would you need to conclude your cross-examination, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At least until the end of today if I cannot be granted any more time tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You'll have that, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But if you could -- we'll see how it proceeds. Let's bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Just for the record, Your Honour, General Karavelic is not a 92 bis witness. This witness was dropped from our witness list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that's what Mr. Karadzic said.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But his statement remains.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think it has anything to do with this witness. Let's get on with the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I apologise for your inconvenience. There was something we need to deal with in your absence. Please make yourself comfortable, General.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We left off discussing the document by the security and intelligence structure. Can you tell us, did this service, security and intelligence service, have its own chain of command in addition to commanders and deputy commanders? Did it have its own chain of command to the top?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did. It was referred to as the professional chain of command, as it were. All the other services had their own respective chains of command and were in touch one with another.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this document admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you say you have translation for this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was told that it seems to exist but it hasn't been uploaded, but for the clarity why don't we mark it for identification for some time. We give the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1374.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Another clarification, please. Do you agree that Jusuf Jusufovic, who was of pro-Yugoslav and pro-JNA orientation was a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to take you back to our discussions during the interview. Do you agree that the structure of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the make-up of it, was more or less a reflection of that in the -- of that in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. It made no sense to change the structure. It was better to simply assume it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that the better part of active-duty officers holding important positions in the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina had originally come from the JNA?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This was definitely true for the corps level. At the level of corps we had former JNA officers. At lower-level commands there were both JNA officers and officers who had not been active-servicemen up to that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were they reserve force officers and officers who were simply more capable than others?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were those who had come from the reserve force as well as those who had not been soldiers but had the requisite qualifications for specific posts. For instance, construction engineer or a mechanical engineer, he could have been in the technical service; an economist could have been assigned to a quartermaster service, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Because of the shortage of time, I have to skip over many topics, although you would have been a precious witness on these issues. You did confirm that as an army you had major difficulties with lower-level commanders, some of whom were outright criminals. For instance, up until the autumn of 1993, Caco and Juka Prazina were commanders and this was a major problem in Sarajevo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's absolutely correct. A number of officers holding commanding positions at crucial points when certain structures were being reorganised or when the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina wanted to introduce order and put in place a proper military structure in keeping with regulations, a decision was made that such commanders should be properly rid of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In November of 1992 you relocated to Sarajevo and became the Chief of Staff of the 1st Corps. You stayed in this position until when exactly in 1993?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Sometime in August 1993, I think mid-August 1993 when I transferred to the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this a promotion?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in our structure, yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Dzambasovic, I would now like to present to you what it is that we know. I will not be referring to all the documents, only the more relevant ones. I will tell you what we knew about the disposition and the infrastructure and the forces of the 1st Corps in Sarajevo proper. Do you agree with me that the 1st Corps deployed some of its forces in the town proper and others in Hrasnica, atop Igman, at Pazarici and Tarcin, and elements of its forces were to the east of Nisici plateau and the general area. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: The 1st Corps had a very broad area of responsibility and included elements of forces in the town and elements of forces in the general area. I think you have that information on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You told us that it wasn't possible to adhere to all the rules of engagement when it came to the evacuation of civilians and infrastructure as well as in positioning headquarters and weapons further away from residential areas; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's absolutely correct. Since the area of responsibility in the town was a very narrow strip, it was impossible to make sure that military units go about their daily business and engage in combat outside of residential areas. It was impossible because of the lay of the ground and because of the way the area of responsibility ran.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. With your assistance I'd like us to go through the situation as it existed during the time when you were Chief of Staff. Please answer with a yes or no or I don't know to save time. Of course you're quite free to say -- to confirm or simply say that that was not the case or that you don't know. Did the 1st Corps have up to 60.000 men in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: According to the information I had, that was roughly the figure, around 60.000 soldiers. There are documents specifically listing the head count as per individual units. This is something that I cannot tell you off the top of my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Under whose command was the special or the guards unit called the Black Swans?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: The unit was part of the 1st Corps and the General Staff. It changed over time but I can't tell you exactly what these times were. But at any rate, it was both a part of the 1st Corps and the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which -- so if the first commander of the armed forces was Sefer Halilovic and then it was Rasim Delic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and before Halilovic there was Hasan Efendic, he was the commander of the republican TO staff. He was replaced by Sefer and he in turn was replaced by Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the command of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina was in the Branica company premises across from the central prison facility in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that General Stjepan Siber, a Croat, and Jovan Divjak, together with their associates, were stationed in the Svjetlost publishing house, across from the town market?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. General Divjak was in the Svjetlost building but General Siber was elsewhere, I can't tell you where exactly or what the -- I know where it is, a couple of -- 300 metres away but I don't know what the name of the building was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But that's at any rate close to the town market where the park dedicated to literary writers is?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: That's close to the JNA hall. The Svjetlost building is across from the town market. Now, Siber was in a building which was close to the JNA hall and I can't recall the name of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It was the Vase Miskina Street now called the Ferhadija street that divided the town marketplace from the JNA hall?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the Main Staff building the Paljike airfield during the war between Visoko and Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: No. It was not finished, although construction works did start.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the 1st Corps of the BH army have within it 15 brigades, and before your arrival there and before you transformed it, it also had several reserve units?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Before I took up my duty there, the corps had several small units. I don't know whether there were 15. I could tell you what they were called. Well, let's say 15 more or less. At a certain point in time, we reorganised the corps in order to amalgamate these units and improve the system of control and command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And this reorganisation coincided with your arrival within the corps?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it happened two or three months later. We carried out this reorganisation together with General Staff members.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The first commander of the 1st Corps was Mustafa Hajrulahovic, was he not, a former JNA officer; and he was replaced by Vahid Karavelic, another former JNA officer. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The Chief of Staff, Asim Dzambasovic, likewise, a former JNA officer; as well as Esad Pelko, Ismet Dahic, Mesud Dzenanovic, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Ismet Dahic was not in the 1st Corps during my time there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have to skip some of these positions. Imsirevic was from the JNA, Ekrem Imsirevic was from the JNA, Dervisevic was from the JNA; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The command of the 1st Corps of the BH army, was it posted in the building of the former Radio Sarajevo across from the Jugobanka building?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's where the command of the 1st Corps was at number 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the operations centre or was the operations centre at the disco in Danijela Ozme street, also number 7?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
