utterances.text: Thank you. Did the -- was the forward command post of the 1st Corps in the building of Visoko in the Siz building in Novo Sarajevo settlement?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: While I was the Chief of Staff -- while I was the Chief of Staff, the 1st Corps did not have a forward command post. After 1994 there was a former -- forward command post in Visoko.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you for the clarification. I would just appreciate the interpreter to correct something. The street is Danijela Ozme Street number 7, across from the Jugobanka building. Is it correct that this street, Danijela Ozme, is some 400 to 500 metres away from the Presidency of Bosnia building?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to list the brigades that existed and were then amalgamated. There was the 1st Muslim Brigade in Buca Potok sector; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: The 1st Muslim was not there. It was the 1st Motorised Brigade. The MTVR means the motorised brigade. PBR stands for mountain brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So the 1st Motorised Brigade was at Bistrik; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: The 1st Mountain Brigade. If you know the garrison command, where that was, it had some facilities, some barracks facilities, which was on the premises or within the perimeter of the former JNA garrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm using the old names and I believe that you assume those same names. So was the 1st Brigade --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please repeat the name of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The interpreters couldn't follow the names of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The 1st Mountain Brigade was, in other words, in the sector Bistrik, the 1st Motorised in Buca Potok sector. Was the 12th Brigade at first in Vogosca and then later it was renamed and became the 111th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: It was in that area, however, not in Vogosca itself but west of Hum in the direction of the traffic engineering faculty and across from the Pretis building, towards Poljane.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was the 2nd Motorised Brigade in the area of Alipasin Most and the neighbourhood of the same name?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was the 3rd Motorised Brigade in Stup?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Later on it was renamed and became the 102nd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was the 4th Motorised Brigade in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was the 3rd Mountain Brigade deployed in Sedrenik area?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It later became 105th Brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was the 5th Motorised -- Mountain Brigade in Dobrinje settlement?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: The 5th Motorised Brigade before March was in Dobrinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was the 6th Mountain Brigade in Hrasno area and Hrasno Brdo?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was in the area of Hrasno Brdo up until the restructuring. After that, together with 105th, it merged with the 105th and became 101st.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was the 7th Mountain Brigade in Kosevo area?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was the 8th Motorised Brigade deployed in the very centre of town near Skenderija?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I have never heard of the 8th. Maybe there was another name but the 8th was certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about the 9th Motorised, was it also down-town?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: That's what was later -- that was later the 105th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the 10th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's the so-called Tarcin Brigade. It was on the northern slopes of Trebevic and Zlatiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The 11th Mountain Brigade, that was in Vasin Han; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that brigade. That may have been before my time, that's the 2nd -- the 152nd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yeah, that's what it became later.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the 13th Specialised Brigade was at Stup; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, probably those small units, all these names, the 13th, I don't know it but probably that's because all those lesser units were later merged into larger units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, talking about the 185th, that was the 2nd Mountain Brigade in 1992. Is it correct that its command post was on the premises of the foreign languages school in Vase Miskina Crni Street number 17?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was in Vase Miskina Street. I didn't know the name of the building itself but it was on Vase Miskina Street, I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: An auxiliary command post was on the premises of the barracks --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch which barracks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that was the logistics unit that was there. They had a forward detachment -- a forward squad deployed elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, later on we are going to show in e-court the composition of 152nd.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 1D3699 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this area? We see the command of the 152nd at Vasa Miskina and on top we see the command of the 3rd Battalion. Is this the area of responsibility of this brigade, the 2nd Mountain Brigade, which later became 152nd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, according to the way it is configured here, yes, although I can't see any command posts that would be denoting that that is the area of responsibility, at least I can't see it shown here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 3686, please, 1D3686.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Would you please date and initial this map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think he needs to sign this because he didn't mark anything. He confirmed as it is and we can admit it as it is.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1375, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see the area of responsibility of the 105th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please take a look at what we have before us now. The areas marked in green, would that be the area of the 105th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, based on the lay of the land, yes, I would say that, although I don't see any indicators there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please take a pen and mark the boundaries of the 105th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please assist the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's difficult to do on this map unless you can show me another map with place names because I don't know how to orientate myself. I don't see how I can -- how I can determine the area of responsibility. You need four points in order to determine an area of responsibility and those points have to be known.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, before this exercise goes any further, we object to the use of this type of Defence-created exhibit, at least it appears to be created from -- by the Defence and contains all kinds of information that we are not able to verify and we don't have the source material for. And as you can see from the witness's answer, he's not entirely comfortable with this map either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like to respond, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a frozen image of something that we represented here, and now I'm asking Mr. Dzambasovic to tell me whether the zone marked with a green line, that is to say, Grdonj, Sedrenik, does that correspond roughly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, I'm not asking you to ask the question. You didn't answer the points Ms. Gustafson raised, how it was created and how they can verify when they have no material to confirm.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's why we have the witness here, to confirm it. Remember that when we watched this we put the cursor on every point and then the document shows up on the basis of which each and every one of these locations was marked. However, Ms. Gustafson was not in the courtroom then, but we believe that the OTP is a single body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you remember the general, General Dzambasovic, stated that he -- it's difficult to do on this map unless you have or you can show me another map with place names because he doesn't know how to orientate himself. Yes, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Just on the accused's point about this being raised before, it was -- this same information in this same format was presented with an earlier witness, protected witness, and we - as Mr. Karadzic points out, the points had references to source material. We've had a chance to look at some of that source material and we do find misrepresentations and inaccuracies. And in addition, we find that the source materials relate to the entire period of the conflict, so there is inconsistencies in the time-frame of the underlying source material. So if that's what this is based on, we have a further objection as to the accuracy and the reliability of this underlying information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You wouldn't have any problem if the Defence is going to produce this map through one of the Defence experts in the future?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: That would certainly be more appropriate, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'll consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber's decision is as follows. We'll mark this map for identification until we are satisfied with its correctness and whether it's consistent with the source material, until we hear from a witness. But until then we'll mark it for identification and proceed with this map and we see how the witness would be able to answer the questions. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you should start -- I don't think the witness will remember the entire question. So you start anew with this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzambasovic, not going into details street by street, this layout of the 105th and 115th on the northern slopes of Trebevic, before it was the 10th Mountain Brigade, then the 152nd, the 111th, the one that you describe from Hum to Vogosca, the 2nd, or rather, the 102nd one and the 1st, and at Stup and so on, does this roughly correspond to what you know as the areas of responsibility of these brigades?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: This map roughly does correspond to that. Since I know these areas very well, I can tell you about the broader area of responsibility where the brigade was in terms of the actual geographic locations involved. Here I don't have particular geographic locations that I can relate to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If this is satisfactory, then let us ask Mr. Dzambasovic to do this on a map that he has kindly marked already, 1D3716, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the meantime we'll give an MFI number for this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI D1376, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the upper right-hand quadrant please be enlarged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: These are your initials here. You initialled this and you marked this on this map in your own time; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could the right-hand third be marked now, the right-hand third of the map. Do we need to zoom in a bit more, Mr. Dzambasovic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: No, not really.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark this now. We see the zone of the 105th, the 152nd, the 115th to the right of this line. Could you please help us and mark it.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: These are command posts and I marked the zones or areas of responsibility for you on the other map, and I think it would be more appropriate if we did that on that other map, the topographic map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we then have this map admitted because it's already been initialled by Mr. Dzambasovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are those writings done by General Dzambasovic? Or whose writing is this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably we need translation, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, otherwise no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll mark this for identification pending English translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1377, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 1D3715. That is also a topographic map that was marked by General Dzambasovic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we need to zoom in or can you confirm the areas of responsibility on the basis of what we see now?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course I can confirm on the basis of what we see now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you like to mark something else?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: There's no need for that, only if you need something.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please then indicate to the Trial Chamber what this map is. You also marked some mortars here and some mechanised -- well, you marked that somewhere, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This disposition of the brigades, not taking into account the changes in names, did it remain more or less the same until the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: In 90 per cent of all cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd just like to put on the record that neither this map nor the prior map were on the list of cross-examination documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You can explain it to me, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I can. When we had our interview with Mr. Dzambasovic in the prison the other night, he was kind enough to offer to take the blank maps and do some homework and put in these markings. And when he arrived here in court just before he began the cross-examination he handed to me the two maps that he had filled in. So we didn't actually have possession of them until a few minutes before his testimony started.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: That would be appropriate for an e-mail to us informing us of that late information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I agree. Pursuant to current practice, the Defence is required to give notice to the Prosecution of the documents it is going to use during the cross-examination before it starts. You can do it -- could have done it a bit earlier. I'm sorry to interrupt the flow of evidence, but if I can ask a question to Ms. Gustafson. In -- with respect to the prior notice you stated that - it's at page 38 of today's transcript: "And if the accused would like to do this in the future I think it would be fair that we have some advance notice that this will be done and all the documents that will be used on these topics falling under Rule 90(H)." In terms of Rule 90(H) line of questioning what do you have in mind in terms of prior notice?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is akin to an examination-in-chief on topics that aren't covered in the Prosecution's evidence favourable to the Defence case. So some kind of advance notice akin to what would be given for direct examination in our view would be appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Does it mean that the Defence is required to reveal their strategy before Prosecution start examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure it would be their strategy, Your Honours, but the simple fact that they will cover certain topics that the Prosecution is now eliciting from the witness and a list of documents they intend to use with the witness. Given that it has nothing to do with the direct examination by the Prosecution, it shouldn't -- nothing that happens in the examination-in-chief by the Prosecution should impact on the way the Defence proceeds under these -- under new topics elicited under Rule 90(H), so I don't see any unfairness there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you like to respond -- I'm sorry to discuss in your presence, but very briefly, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I think this is a situation where when a witness comes here we don't know the scope of his knowledge and we didn't learn of it until our interview with him as to whether it would be advisable to his ask him these kinds of questions. At the interview, Ms. Gustafson was present so she heard all of the same things that she's hearing now. But in any event there is no rule that requires us to make that kind of disclosure, but I think as a matter of practice we could certainly attempt to do that in the future. If we know we're going to examine a witness on topics outside of the scope, we can try to at least give whatever kind of notice we have to the Prosecution. I don't have any problem in doing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's carry on, Mr. Karadzic. Have we admitted this one? So we'll admit this and -- but we'll mark it for identification pending English translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1378, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the 1st Battalion of this 152nd, or rather, 2nd Brigade had its command post in an abandoned house by Piljina Kafana at Vasin Han?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether that was an abandoned house. The 1st Battalion -- now, where did it have its command post somewhere in Faletici. Which house that is, I don't know, but I know that it is in the area of Faletici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The 2nd Battalion in the Jajce barracks?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The 3rd Battalion, the command post was also in the Jajce barracks?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that I don't know, whether it was in the Jajce barracks because its location was a bit risky. I think it was only the 2nd one that was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The Mixed artillery battalion had its command post in the Zmajevac barracks about a kilometre and a half or 2 kilometres away from Podhrastovi; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Whose mixed artillery battalion?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Of the 152nd.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: The 152nd did not have a mixed artillery battalion, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At the time when you were there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And not even later. I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: M-A-D, is that what it was called?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. I think that's a mistake, you're mistaken there. Within the 1st Corps there was a light artillery battalion of the PVO. LAD PVO, that would be the abbreviation, and that was in the area of the Zmajevac barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. They had one howitzer of 105-millimetres on the training-grounds of the Zmajevac barracks; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: No, that I don't know. That is too small for the Chief of Staff of a corps. I really didn't go into each and every artillery piece.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that the logistics units was in Jajce barracks and in the Injis cafeteria, which used to be the Herzegovina restaurant near the cathedral where the officer cadre went for their meals?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: It is correct that the brigade command took their meals at this restaurant. Now, as for their logistics battalion, I don't know where that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that this restaurant is in the square between the cathedral and the Vase Miskina Crni Street which is now the Ferhadija Street?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So yes, to be more precise, it's on the corner of the street. Now, did you know that the BH army had a special MUP unit attached to it called Lasta, which together with the Black Swans, Crni Labudovi, a special unit of the Main Staff participated in joint operations?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, from time to time that unit took part together in combat with the Black Swans unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now just go quickly through the positions of the 105th which was earlier known as the 9th Mountain Brigade. Was the command post of this brigade in the Sipad building in Trampina Street, next to the central park.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was the alternative command post at the Ivan Cankar elementary school as well as the rear command post?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I have no idea where that school is, but, no, they did not have a forward command post. The 9th only had a command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here it says an alternative command post?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. The forward -- well, maybe it was a rear command post, maybe that's what this is a reference to. There's something that is not quite clear there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did this brigade -- was this brigade in its entirety deployed, as we saw a little earlier in the Sedrenik area up to Grdonj, and that it had its lines at Grdonj below Spicasta Stijena, so were they in this area?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, when you say "here," do you mean this map?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it says on the map "105th."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, below that, within the golden line, would you agree, General Dzambasovic, that this was the area of responsibility of the 105th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In general terms, yes, this would be the area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The image that we showed earlier, did it correspond roughly to this, our image?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the one without any geographic names? Yes, it would -- it approximates that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that its area of responsibility was at Hladivode, where it linked up with the 152nd, then Mala Brda, Rijeka Potok and Kobilja Glava?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: That was the defence line that you just described.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That was the area facing the enemy, right, the army of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now take a look at 1D3689, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we are waiting for it to come up, do you agree that this brigade had up to seven battalions, four motorised, one MAD, one logistics battalion, an engineer battalion, sabotage, and reconnaissance company, a military police company, and an anti-nuclear, biological, and chemical weapons company?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: The establishment structure of these brigades is probably -- contained these units. However, I don't know the lower-level units within this brigade. I don't know what exactly they were. However, none of these subordinate units was fully manned as it should be per establishment. In other words, not a single brigade had an artillery unit. They had artillery weapons, but a unit that was prescribed by the establishment, there was not a single brigade in the town that had that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can you see in this map of the city, can you recognise where the area of responsibility was of the 105th Brigade? You see that we have the Kosevo stadium there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it. Well, this roughly corresponds to its area of responsibility. Again, we don't have any geographic features, but based on these facilities and some of the buildings that are shown there, I could confirm that this is roughly the area of responsibility of the 105th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: We have the same objections to this map as the previous Defence-created map. There appear to be locations marked here and we don't have the underlying information. If the information is what was provided previously in the earlier presentation then we have concerns about its reliability.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: All that Defence did in relation to this map was to mark -- indicate or locate the -- some or command posts of the alleged 105th Brigade and we heard the evidence from the witness that those locations are roughly corresponding to the location. Do we need some expert witness in relation to this further?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I understood the witness's answer to be that this roughly - roughly - corresponded to the area of responsibility of the 105th Brigade, and again he had concerns about the nature of the map and his ability to identify that area of responsibility. He did not confirm, as far as I could see, the locations of these command posts it seems to be of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: General, can I ask you this: By answering, "Well, this roughly corresponds to its area of responsibility," did you mean that the locations indicated as the command posts are -- approximately correspond to the actual locations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you clarify. What did you mean by "area of responsibility"? While -- because we did -- do not see any area of responsibility in this map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We cannot see it from this map, but we said that this red line is a kind of border, and visually, I guessed that this is roughly the area of responsibility of the 105th Brigade. However, the command posts -- all I know for sure is that the brigade command post was in Trampina Street in that building that was mentioned earlier. As for all the other command posts of the subordinate units, I'm not sure where they were, nor did I confirm that these were indeed those locations. I'm not sure where the command posts of those lower units, those subordinate units, were. In other words, the area of responsibility is a larger area which has a certain depth and width, and within that area you would deploy commands and units. And roughly speaking, this does correspond to that area of responsibility. But as for the precise locations of the posts, command posts, of subordinate units within the zone, that I don't know. I don't know where they are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given the weight of the evidence if admitted, the Chamber sees no point of admitting this with this witness. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Then we will try to make this more visible and use it on some other occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, do you recall that the 1st Battalion had a command post in a private home near Mehina Kafana? You must have known that; we all know where Mehina Kafana is, Mehin's Cafe.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I know where Mehina Kafana is but that was not where the command post was. It was at the meteorological building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The command post of the 2nd Battalion was at the seismological agency; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: That's why I told you that I didn't know the deployment of subordinate units and I'm not absolutely certain where they were and that's why I cannot give you any precise information about the deployments and the areas where the subordinate units were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know by any chance whether the command post of the 3rd Battalion was in the kindergarten building?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was the command post of the 4th Battalion at the physical education faculty at Kosevo?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the command post of the reconnaissance and sabotage company was -- it used to be at Juvala Nitraka street and then later on it was at the bakeries in Breka?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't know and I've never been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the command post of the engineering battalion was in the Jazija Omanovic elementary school building?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that the command post of the logistics battalion was at the Ivan Cankar elementary school and then later moved to Bosna export company on Romanijska Street?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know of any logistics units and where they were deployed and I wasn't really interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that the military police company was in Pcelica kindergarten in Svetozara Markovica Street?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to talk about the 1st Motorised Brigade. Do you know where it was deployed, the 1st Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I know where -- what its area of responsibility was and where its command post was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was the command post in Bosna Lijek -- in the building Bosna Lijek and then later on moved to the Magros building in Blagoja Parovica Street?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I only know about the Magros building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was the rear command post in Pofalici on the premises of the prison there and then later on moved to Marsal Tito barracks?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were the command posts 1 and 2 in Zivkovici village, on Zuc, and 2 on Orlic hill?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: While I was the Chief of Staff of the 1st Corps, the forward command post of the 1st Brigade was in Jezera village, that was south of the Zuc hill, some 200 to 300 metres away. As for the other locations I'm not aware it was ever there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about the command post number 3, do you know it was in Velesici next to the repair shop --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot follow at this speed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could slow down; interpreters couldn't follow. Could you repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The third command post of this brigade, was it in Velesici 100 metres from the new repair shop, auto repair shop, the trig points X 58025 and Y 32650?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I already said that I don't know the deployments and the positions of those subordinate units and it was not really within my competence. I was not even supposed to know. I was not required to know their locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I will skip the lower-level units and let's move on to brigade level. Do you know that the 2nd Motorised Brigade as it was called earlier was later renamed and became the 111th Motorised Brigade, whereas the 95th became the Vitez Brigade or the Viteska Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, no. That was the 1st Brigade, the 1st was later called the 111th that we just mentioned. And then later on it was renamed again and it was called the Viteska Brigade or Knight Brigade or the Glorious, I think that was the name that it was given, but I'm not sure which of the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was its area of responsibility between Miljacka River, Astro factory, over the Zuc hill to the north towards Vogosca?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: The area of responsibility of the 1st, or rather, the 111th Brigade was between the Zuc hill running to the north-east towards the transportation technical faculty, via Slatina village, Kromolj, and then Grdonj -- I'm sorry, I got confused. Via Slatina village. So that's the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then towards the centre of town it went all the way to the Astro factory where the 154th had its command post?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: You've confused it. The 1st Brigade, or rather, the 101st had a command post in Magros and the second one, I think it was the 112th, had its command post at this location that you just referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dzemala Bijedica 144, opposite Astro; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, that's the second one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I'm not going to ask you about the firing positions of this brigade either. Can we now have a look at the 102nd Brigade and where it was. Before it was called the 3rd Motorised Brigade or perhaps I've confused that too?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was it in the area of Stup from the wire factory, Alipasino Polje towards Stup, towards Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: It had its command post at the wire factory and it defended the area towards Stup, or rather, part of the student dormitories in Nedzarici and then all the way down to the Energoinvest factory called TAT and then the area to the north-west towards Rajlovac, that is to say moving from Stup to Rajlovac to that underpass roughly, that's where it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In Vladimir Peric Valter at Stup was there an alternative command post there and was there a forward command post at the Lav restaurant?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I went to that first facility that you referred to, that was the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. While following this line of evidence, can we see the exhibit D1377 so that we can follow a bit more easily. Please proceed. That's the marked position of the ABiH marked by this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. That would really help us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So we can see here where you marked the command post of the 102nd, that is Valter Peric; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I think it is at Stup. I don't know which building exactly but it was in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about the 1st Battalion, the command of the 1st Battalion, was it at the elementary school Pavle Goranin and the forward command post at a private house in Stup, which I believe you decided on through one of your orders?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: It's possible that that's what I did, but as for the deployment of these lower-ranking units, I really don't know. Quite simply, I happen to know some of them but I don't know this one.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, do you believe it would be useful if we asked the general to mark roughly with this electronic pen the area of the 2nd Brigade to the best of his knowledge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If he can. Just -- could you wait -- would you like to ask to zoom in this map further?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If possible, that would be good.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The left-hand third.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: General, could you wait a bit further till assisted by our usher. Mr. Karadzic asked to zoom in to mark the 2nd Brigade. We see a number 2 there. Yes. I think that's sufficient. Could you wait -- could you wait.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Can I mark it now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please do. You marked the tank, right, you marked the forward command posts. Can you roughly mark the area of responsibility of the 2nd or the 3rd or the 102nd?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks] That would be it roughly. The area of responsibility of the 102nd Brigade that goes from the Miljacka River towards the Dobrinja river, that is to say --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: South.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: From the north to the south.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And on the north?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. The 2nd is up there. It's above the road leading through Rajlovac, that is to say to the north of the road to Rajlovac is the 2nd Motorised. And to the south of the road to Rajlovac is the area of the 102nd.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask you to please hand over this drawing to the general, and if he accepts it. [In English] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, perhaps there could be some explanation. It's unclear what this document is and we've never seen it before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's from our map that we created. It's just supposed to jog Mr. Dzambasovic's memory so that he remembers whether that's the way it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can do it electronically as well. It has a number. It can be called up -- actually, no, the ELMO is better. I'd be sorry to lose the one that we have here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this help you mark the borders on the electronic map, or rather, the boundaries of the 102nd?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: It would be easy for me to tell you all of that if I just had the names that I referred to a moment ago. The names cannot be seen here. You just see the buildings marked there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the rest of the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you were to call up 1D3696 you would see every one of the names?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if that's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the meantime why don't we ask the witness to sign and date the current marked map as it is now. General, could you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter could not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The 22nd I think.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We keep this map. Should we give it a number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D1379, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We have a break and come back to this issue after the break. We resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Where were we? Could we upload the last map marked by the witness, D1379? General, I don't think I've fully understood the meaning of these markings. Could you explain to us again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are tactical signs used by the former JNA and taken on by the BH army. These are tactical signs representing brigade command posts. Wherever you have this sign it stands for a command post of the brigade. It's an area where the command staff of a brigade is stationed. And - excuse me - these are the various facilities housing command posts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I meant the black line you marked just now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The black line, well that's an approximation of the area of responsibility of the 102nd Brigade. These are roughly the boundaries of the area of responsibility. Though admittedly I did make the same markings on the topographical map and I should perhaps not have done the same thing here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I understand. Back to you, Mr. Karadzic. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I do understand that you would not be familiar with the battalion command posts since you were higher up, but do you know that it was in the Djokic primary school that the 2nd Battalion of the Brigade was stationed whereas the manoeuvre battalion was in a kindergarten at Cengic Vila?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as I speak I don't know the location of either the school or the kindergarten.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The 155th or the 5th, did you mark its location in the centre of Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know the name of the street but I do know the building where it was housed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was it in the Sipad building in the Mitsubishi avenue?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the name of the street but it is the Sipad building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps you could make another marking on the same map and we'll admit it, the area of responsibility of the 5th Brigade in the Dobrinja neighbourhood with the exception of the airport neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I did mark the area of responsibility on that other map because we have place names there, and I did orient myself in making the markings with respect to the place names that I don't have on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you. Did this brigade have two special units Hazet Hamza [phoen] and El Fatih?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. It's the first time I'm hearing these names.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know how many battalions there were in the 1st, later 105th, Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it had four battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You don't know, do you, the composition of the mortar batteries and artillery and armoured assets of the 105th?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think the 105th had any of these assets, and I did emphasize that none of the brigades had an armoured or anti-tank unit or an artillery unit by their very establishment. Some of the brigades had artillery pieces. Only one brigade, the 1st one, 111th, had several tanks, most of which were in a state of disrepair because there were no spare parts to repair them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I attract your attention to the area of responsibility of the 101st Brigade, its command post, it was formerly the 1st Brigade, or rather, the 6th Mountain Brigade. It was set up as the 6th Mountain Brigade for Hrasno?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It became the 101st. Its command post was in the Viktor Bubanj barracks where the court of Bosnia-Herzegovina is housed today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The first commander was Nedzad Ajnadzic a JNA officer who later became a commander of the 1st Corps or the 11th Division?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: He was the brigade commander and he replaced Karavelic as the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did General Ajnadzic write a book about the defence of Sarajevo and the combat that took place within Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can all the participants see the markings in respect of the 101st or should we ask the witness to mark the location?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: This is where the 101st Brigade was situated, that's the Viktor Bubanj barracks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We see it so we can proceed, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that these markings indicate the brigade command posts of the 1st, 2nd, 101st, 102nd, 5th, and the forward command post of the 2nd, this is the area where we have the small flag, slightly dented, but it is not a triangle. It's rather a dented rhomboid.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: What's your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In this part of the map can we see the command posts of the HVO, Kralj Tomislav, is that right, that's the command post of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was housed in a primary school building. I don't know its name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And west of that location is the command post of the 1st Motorised Brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, at Magros.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Next we have the 2nd Motorised further west, which is in the Astra area?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the 102nd.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The 102nd is close to the television, is it right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: It's -- the 102nd was housed in the wire factory, wire and cables factory. Well, I know it was in that particular compound. I'm not sure about the very building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then we have the two forward command posts of the 2nd and the 102nd and then we have the command post of the 5th?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now see the eastern part of town, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably we need to upload D1378.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like to direct your attention to the 10th Mountain Brigade, later renamed 115th; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I think that the 10th and the 1st formed the 115th at a later stage. While I was the chief of the corps staff it was the 10th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And its area of responsibility ran from the river Miljacka to the south, including the northern slopes of Trebevic and up until the positions of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, all the way to Zlatiste and the Vrace monument beyond the Jewish cemetery, that area, stretching on towards Zlatiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Not Slatina, Zlatiste. Could you please indicate for us with a cursor, we can see Vrace, can we not, in the direction of the 101st we see Vrace and the monumental complex there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we can see it, though I can't make it clearly. Perhaps we could zoom in a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Cicin Han, Mrakusa, Kovacici, all the way to Vrbanja, all of that was covered within the area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, roughly the area you just indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: General -- yes. Now is it better?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is much better now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Don't touch it, please, wait until assisted. Yes. Would you like the general to mark something, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'd appreciate it if the general could mark the area between the Vrbanja bridge and the VRS positions all the way to Miljacka and the 115th Brigade positions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And all the way up there to Vidikovac; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: This is roughly the area of responsibility south of the Miljacka which covers Soukbunar, Skenderija, Bostarici, and the neighbourhood of Cicin Han Lipa. This is roughly the area of responsibility of the 10th Mountain Brigade. Now, north-east of the area along the length of the Miljacka, including the quarry - which you know where it is - this section of the Stari Grad municipality south of the river Miljacka is the area of responsibility of the 1st Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And when they merged it all became the area of responsibility of the 115th; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it became the area of responsibility of the 115th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You marked the brigade command post as located in the command of the 2nd Military District?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the command was not housed in that building. It's beyond that. There was a ground floor structure, prefabricated structure, which housed the command of the 10th Brigade. Now, the very building of the 2nd Military District is some 20 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you think whether Carrington 2 on the 6th of April square where the 2nd Battalion was housed at the -- it had -- that the 5th Battalion had its forward command post there, you can tell us if you don't know?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: No, I told you already that I can't testify to the location of the command posts of the units of a lower level.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the map admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And if you could place your initials and date the map, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be done.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1380, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we stay with the map for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we see the HVO Kralj Tvrtko Brigade on the edge of the map, can you see that there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was housed in a school building. I don't know the name of the school. That was the command post of the HVO brigade precisely where I marked it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the artillery brigade of the 1st Corps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Unfortunately the Registry has lost the previous marking. If necessary, we'll ask the witness to kindly to mark those lines again if you wish, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the area of responsibility of the 10th and 1st, which later merged into 115th. This is what the general is well aware of. It's where Kovacici and Grbavica are located, the Vrbanja bridge, Cicin Han and everything else that came under the area of responsibility. It's the western boundary, is it not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is of the 1st Brigade and this is of the 10th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Previously you marked some lines to the right of this map, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did that now as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's the right-hand side boundary of the 1st which later became 115th; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The northern boundary runs along the river. That's why I didn't mark it. I wanted the map to be as clear as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did we save it or did we lose it again? There seems to be a technical difficulty but whether we can use the video image -- yes, we will use that. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have 1D3613 just for a moment so that you can confirm for us, perhaps, the HVO command posts. Do you agree that the HVO is actually a Croatian military formation, or rather, a formation, military formation, of the Croatian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina that fought within the BH army at the time?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: The HVO brigade in Sarajevo was within the 1st Corps of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, whereas the HVO units outside of Sarajevo, many of them rather, were not within the BH army. They were a separate formation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D3683, please. This is not it. 1D3683.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The command of Kralj Tvrtko Brigade was there, was the command of the battalion here and the command of the company there. This company was facing the Serb part of Grbavica; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: The command was at the school that I showed you a moment ago. For a while it was deployed from Skenderija towards Elektroprivreda that is to say on the right bank of the Miljacka, or rather, from Marin Dvor by the national museum and then to Elektroprivreda, roughly that is where its area of responsibility was, in that territory. That's where this brigade was deployed. In fact, it was a smaller unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please mark Marin Dvor here and then -- and then the western boundary. You see where Marin Dvor is? You see where the Assembly and government building is, where it says command of the 3rd Battalion, is that it? And then the trams, remember that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I can't find it yet. I can't identify it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, please. You seem to be very persistent in using this kind of map. Yes, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The same problems arise with this map. The witness can only confirm the brigade command posts that he has already marked on another map. He hasn't confirmed these other locations that the Defence have indicated on this map for which we have no source information. And if Mr. Karadzic intends to have the witness mark this map, I'd just like to indicate now that we would object to its admission because of this unsourced and unsubstantiated information contained within it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is rather simple or simpler than compared to other ones. This is a Google map and he placed for locations -- we haven't heard a question in relation to this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understood the -- that Mr. Karadzic asked for confirmation of these command posts and the witness answered that he could only confirm the command post of the brigade which he had already marked. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: -- from his answer I understood that he could not confirm the other locations which is where my concerns arise from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He didn't ask about other posts, and rather he proceeded to ask the witness to mark Marin Dvor.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: At line --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic --

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: -- sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- I would like you to proceed with your next point.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you haven't identified Marin Dvor but if you look at the bifurcation where it says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, the witness has marked location of the command post of the HVO brigade. I don't see a further point of -- further exploring with this witness on this point. Why don't you move to your next topic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We can do that, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now see Hrasnica, however, on the map that -- just a moment, please. Let's see which is going to be the best-suited map for that. 1D3716 -- I beg your pardon, 3715 would be better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit D1378.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The southern third, the lower third, could that be enlarged, please, a bit more than this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, did you mark in yellow the zone of responsibility of the 4th Motorised Brigade that was later named the 104th and had its area of responsibility from Hrasnica to Sokolovic Kolonija, Butmir, all the way to the airport runway?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's the area of responsibility approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The Butmir end of the tunnel was also within its area of responsibility; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: The exit from Sarajevo was on the Butmir side, that is to say the exit from the tunnel was in the area of responsibility of the 4th, or rather, 104th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was the command post of the brigade in the building of the new post office in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: It was in the building, but I don't know whether it's the new post office. I just know which building it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that the alternate command post was in Stanogradnja and the forward command post in Vrhovi, the road up on the hill?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: This alternative command post, as you call it, I don't know. But at Hrasnicki Stan that's where the forward command post was, between the mountains of Igman and Hrasnica there is a macadam road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It would be very helpful if you knew the command posts of the lower-ranking units, for example, the 3rd Battalion in Sokolovic Kolonija, the supermarket, the command post of the 4th in the cultural centre in Butmir. Did you know that, the command post of the 2nd in the hotel, or rather, in the second high-rise near the post office in Hrasnica, did you know that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: No. I did not even tour these lower-ranking commands. This I know because I personally went to the commands of all the brigades. As for battalion commands, I hardly ever went to battalion commands.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This has already been admitted, this map, so I don't think -- well, to the south of Hrasnica, is that where Mount Igman is and further south do we have Mount Bjelasnica and was this taken by the 100 or the 4th Brigade of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and kept throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, to the south of Hrasnica is Mount Igman and even further south Mount Bjelasnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was the artillery of the 1st Corps on Mount Igman, the artillery that was not in the city itself?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: In the city itself there wasn't any artillery. I've said that. These were individual artillery pieces. Out of town there was artillery, especially in the area of Igman, because that was the most favourable position for such weaponry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: General, if you could tell us the difference between artillery and individual artillery pieces. We are not experts on the artillery.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was asked whether artillery units were there. An artillery unit cannot be a single artillery piece or just two artillery pieces. There weren't any such units in the city, that is to say that the smallest formation in the artillery is an artillery platoon. It has four artillery pieces up to six, depending on the type. And then there is a battery and then there is an artillery battalion, and so on. So within the city itself --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, that's sufficient. In the interpretation we didn't hear the word "unit," so that's sufficient. Let's proceed, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know of the composition of that artillery brigade on Mount Igman?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: According to establishment, there wasn't an artillery brigade on Mount Igman. It didn't have that much equipment. Roughly, that unit was at the rank of an artillery battalion, that is to say it should be around 16 to 18 artillery pieces of different calibre and for different purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: From 90-millimetres up to 105-, 122-, 155-; right? Howitzers.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: In principle, those are artillery pieces, everything you mentioned just now. Now, as for the types that were there, I really cannot say, I don't know. But there was a unit that was roughly at the level of an artillery battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 16 pieces approximately?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All of the valley of Sarajevo including Pale, was it within the range of these artillery pieces?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Only 152-millimetre cannons and 130-millimetre guns, according to technical tactical characteristics with special ammunition had a range of over 20 kilometres. As far as I know, the army had only two 152-millimetre guns in this area. All other artillery pieces did not have a range that exceeded 10 to 15 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us now identify locations where combat equipment was manufactured. Do you remember a centre called CNP was established?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Of course I knew as Chief of Staff this centre, except that I never went there, but I know that something was being manufactured in the factory called Vaso Miskin Crni and some equipment was manufactured in the factory called Zrak. That is a factory of the former JNA, a factory manufacturing optical instruments.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we'll like to go through these locations. Let us just see whether Faik Kulovic was chief and Berko Zekovic deputy chief for the production base Mirko Greho?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know either one of them, I really don't. So the field of logistics is something that we staff officers were not exactly interested in. This was mostly done by officers from the logistics sector. I only knew by way of information that something was being manufactured at these two facilities. What we were interested in was whether we had that for when we needed it or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I just remind you of some of these things and then you can tell me whether you know that or not. Was there any production at the faculty of mechanical engineering?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about explosive charges for grenades, was that ongoing at the tobacco factory?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: This is the first I've ever heard of it, although I never entered the factory compound during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the Astra factory were shells and grenades also filled with explosives?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know where that factory is and I haven't heard of that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about the wire factory, did you hear that it was used for this kind of manufacturing?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I know the wire factory, I've already said that to you a moment ago, that was the command of the 102nd Brigade, but for that kind of manufacturing I was not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You know about Zrak?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sighting devices and the like?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At the faculty of chemistry?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the Vaso Miskin Crni factory equipment for shells of 60 and 82 millimetres?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: The only thing I know about that factory is that some shells were manufactured there, but I never entered the premises either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Also explosives at the Sarajevo brewery?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The manufacturing of footwear for soldiers at Kozni Kombinat Visoko in the Marsal Tito Street?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know about this kind of manufacturing of textiles and other equipment that was needed by the quartermaster corps but I never visited these locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The factory Alhos, did they manufacture uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: It is possible that uniforms were manufactured at Alhos but not just military uniforms because I think that there was not sufficient -- there weren't any fabrics for that purpose so I think that they used the fabrics that they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in Hrasnica, between two high-rises, mortars were manufactured in workshops?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the military -- the defence industry from before was at Saniteks which produced various types of shells, up to 700 pieces per day, the factory of medical equipment and medicines?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Bosna Lijek and Saniteks, as the name suggests, it is normal to expect them to produce medical equipment and, or rather, medical supplies and medicines and this is the first time I hear that they also manufactured other resources.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Feroelektro, did you know that it manufactured spare parts for artillery pieces and ammunition?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that Feroelektro was destroyed, so I don't think -- I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll skip the less-prominent such factories or places of production. Is it correct that the 4th Motorised Brigade and the Pazarici and Tarcin units later merged and became the 14th Division which belonged to the 1st Corps but was outside the town centre itself?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Those units did merge to become a division and the division was formed by the command, or rather, the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will no longer insist. You told us what you knew.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just ask, I believe this map has already been admitted into evidence so we don't have to tender it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. It has been admitted already. Just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, of course we did mark it for identification pending the translation of those legends.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now quickly see D339, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the 5th of February, 1993, you were the Chief of Staff within the 1st Corps, correct, that was your position?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this an order from the commander, Mustafa Hajrulahovic, Talijan, an order to disband the mixed artillery rocket brigade of the 1st Corps in Sarajevo and to distribute those resources and send them to other units. So a 120-millimetre mortar battery is being sent to the 3rd Motorised Brigade; a 105-millimetre howitzer battery is sent to the 1st Motorised Brigade; a self-propelled howitzer battery with all personnel and materiel technical means is to be sent to the 6th Motorised Brigade; the command reconnaissance battery to be deployed within four rocket units and so on. So do you recall that this was an order to reorganise the part of the corps?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. This was part of the restructuring, but as I mentioned earlier it says here "disband the mixed artillery rocket brigade," but you can see when you look below where it says "battery, battery, battery," that those weren't -- that wasn't really a brigade. As I've already said, the 1st Corps did not have a single unit that was of brigade level. We called it -- we called them brigades, but in fact they did not have the equipment and the weapons that would qualify them as brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This has already been admitted into evidence. It's a D exhibit. Can we now have 1D3706. Can you confirm that what we see in the lower left third, there is Grdonj Brdo and then Spicasta Stijena next to it, we see some trenches, communication trenches, both above and below?
